questions.question: What mathematical set represents steady-state feasible fluxes under the paper's model?

options.A: The affine solution manifold Sν=b intersected with the flux box 0≤ν≤νmax
options.B: The null space of S without bounds
options.C: A simplex defined only by biomass-maximizing fluxes
options.D: The set of all positive metabolite concentrations

questions.rationale: Mass balance defines an affine subspace; bounds cut out a convex polytope.

questions.question: Why can the authors treat the steady-state flux subspace as dimension N−M?

options.A: They assume every reaction is independent
options.B: They assume the stoichiometric matrix has full row rank M after dependent equations are removed
options.C: They set all M metabolite concentrations to zero

questions.rationale: After removing linearly dependent equations, rank(S)=M and the solution manifold has dimension N−M.

questions.question: What role does λ=det(λ̂†λ̂)^(1/2) play in their sub-dimensional volume definition?

options.A: It is the BP normalization constant for every variable message
options.B: It is the determinant of the stoichiometric matrix
options.C: It is the constant Jacobian factor inducing Euclidean measure on the affine space
options.D: It rescales each flux maximum to one

questions.rationale: The induced measure includes the Jacobian of the linear parametrization.

questions.question: What exact benchmark was used for comparing the BP approximation with LRS?

options.A: 1000 E. coli knockouts with N=120 and M=40
options.C: A single full-rank network with 1024 metabolites
options.D: 1000 random diluted stoichiometric matrices with N=12, M=4 and fluxes bounded between 0 and 1

questions.rationale: The low-dimensional benchmark used 1000 instances at N=12,M=4, qmax=1024.
questions.evidence_quote: generated 1000 realizations of random stoichiometric matrices with N = 12, M = 4

questions.question: What accuracy trend did the authors observe as qmax increased in the low-dimensional BP/LRS test?

options.A: Finer message discretization improved the approximation quality
options.C: The approximation became exact only at qmax=16

questions.rationale: The relative-error histograms improved with finer bins.

questions.question: What was the computational comparison between LRS and BP as network size grew?

options.A: BP was faster only for N<4, then both became exponential
options.B: LRS was faster through about N≈12, then its time rose exponentially while BP remained modest and nearly linear
options.C: LRS stayed polynomial to N=120 while BP became exponential
options.D: Both methods had identical scaling across all tested sizes

questions.rationale: The paper reports a crossover near twelve fluxes and divergent scaling thereafter.
questions.evidence_quote: LRS outperforms BP up to sizes N ∼ 12 where the running time of LRS explodes exponentially while BP maintains a modest almost-linear behavior.

questions.question: What preprocessing produced the E. coli genome-scale network used for average-flux analysis?

options.A: Removed all reactions involving ATP and ADP and retained 626 metabolites
options.B: Kept only metabolites with connectivity >40 and maximized biomass
options.C: Removed fractional-stoichiometry reactions and metabolites with connectivity >40, then checked for one-sided metabolites
options.D: Reduced the original network to 40 metabolites and 74 internal reactions

questions.rationale: They transformed the 1035-reaction, 626-metabolite model into a sparse matrix after those removals and consistency checks.
questions.evidence_quote: we obtain a matrix with 1005 re- actions and 560 metabolites.

questions.question: How did the central-metabolism knockout simulation alter a knocked-out reaction's allowed maximum flux?

options.B: Set only the knocked-out flux to zero
options.C: Reduced the flux maximum by 25 units
options.D: Reduced it to 0.25 of its original value while keeping other maxima at 1

questions.rationale: The simulated knockout used one-quarter of the original maximum.

questions.question: Which reactions/pathway pattern was associated with the strongest solution-space entropy decreases after knockouts?

options.A: Low-redundancy glycolysis reactions and selected citric-cycle reactions such as FUM and ACONT
options.D: Only ATP and ADP exchange fluxes

questions.rationale: The reactions with ΔS<−3 clustered in low-redundancy glycolysis and some Krebs-cycle reactions.
questions.evidence_quote: Most of them are associated with the glycolysis pathway

questions.question: What limitation did the authors explicitly place on extending the method to nonlinear constraints?

options.A: The method cannot handle any bounds on flux
options.B: Each constraint should involve only a small number of variables
options.D: Only constraints involving all fluxes simultaneously are allowed

questions.rationale: They suggest broader functional constraints are possible provided each involves few variables.
questions.evidence_quote: provided that the number of variables involved in each of the constraints remains small
